name: glass-lens
summary: Glass plates over a soft pastel scene: each one blurs and lifts the colour behind it, catches light on its rim, and bends the scene inward near its edge like a thick slab, with a slight colour split. The rim bend is an SVG displacement map inside backdrop-filter (Chromium); elsewhere the plates stay plain CSS glass.

rim.description: Widest the refracting rim gets, in CSS pixels. Small plates narrow it to their short side / 3.5. Upstream's rim.

edge.description: How far inward the very edge samples the scene, in rim widths. Upstream's edge.

power.description: How fast the bend falls off across the rim: (1 - d / rim) ^ power. Upstream's power.

dispersion.description: How much further red bends than blue at the rim; 0 for a single pass with no colour split. Upstream's dispersion.

deviations.what: The scene behind the glass is a CSS stand-in (--fx-scene): soft stripes over radial washes in the light colours of upstream's mesh wallpaper.
deviations.why: Upstream shows its glass over WebGL wallpapers, photos and Apple wallpaper files its NOTICE says must not be redistributed. A section library ships no imagery and no second renderer, so the scene is one CSS background a site author can point at their own picture. The stripes are there so the rim has edges to bend.

deviations.what: Every custom property gains the --fx- prefix, .glass becomes .fx-glens__glass, and lens.js writes --fx-glass-lens instead of --glass-lens.
deviations.why: Seam. paw-fx custom properties are --fx- prefixed, and a bare .glass class or --ink property would collide with host-page CSS.

deviations.what: No @property registrations, no material transitions, no Safari redraw toggle (--redraw), and no playground rules (.stage[data-refract], .stage[data-tuning], [data-engine=webkit]). --fx-density, --fx-keep and --fx-floor are set on each plate instead.
deviations.why: Those exist so the playground can glide between presets, swap in its WebGL refraction and work around its own Safari surfaces. A section has one fixed material, so its plates carry the values the registrations gave as initial values.

deviations.what: No adapt.js: plates do not sample the scene to pick their tint density or switch to dark glass.
deviations.why: Adaptive tint samples the wallpaper's pixels, which needs a canvas or video under the glass. The CSS scene has none, so density is a fixed --fx-density per plate (1 on the copy card, upstream's 0.35 elsewhere) and dark glass is opt-in with data-kind="dark".

deviations.what: lens.js's export keywords are dropped and mount() gives each .fx-glens__glass its own liquidGlass() lens, setting data-fx-live once the first filter is in place.
deviations.why: Seam. A paw-fx effect is one index.js exporting mount and meta; the registry ships no sibling module, so the lens is inlined rather than imported.
